title: A vector index in the browser
subtitle: How much each vector takes and when exact search stops working
mission: Index the 12 chunks of Aurora’s handbook with real embeddings on your device and search them. Then scale up and find out when the index no longer fits in the browser.

predict.question: 12 chunks × 384 dimensions × 4 bytes per number. How big is the index?

feedback.right: right: 12 × 384 × 4 = 18,432 bytes. A whole handbook fits easily in the browser; the embedding model (~120 MB) weighs far more than the index.
feedback.wrong: it’s about 18 KB: 12 × 384 × 4 = 18,432 bytes. A vector is small; what grows is the count.
feedback.skipped: no guess? Run it and check the memory.

coach.ui: guess noted. Run with scale at 12. For real embeddings, pick "In the browser" (~120 MB, once).
coach.cmd: guess noted. Run index with --scale 12; switch the executor in the scene for real embeddings.

tryNext.ui: Ask "How long before should I tell them I’ll take time off?": no words in common with the vacation chunk, and it still comes first.
tryNext.cmd: Run index "How long before should I tell them I’ll take time off?" and look at the first chunk.

why.simples:
Each handbook chunk becomes a list of 384 numbers summarizing its meaning. Storing that is cheap: the whole handbook takes less than a photo.
To search, the question becomes numbers too and we compare it with every chunk. With millions of chunks, comparing one by one gets slow and heavy.
why.dev:
Memory ≈ vectors × dimensions × 4 bytes (float32), plus metadata and text. Exact (brute-force) search compares the query with every vector: perfect, but O(n·d).
In the browser, up to tens of thousands of chunks work fine in memory (or IndexedDB). Beyond that, use a server-side vector database with an approximate (ANN) index such as HNSW: pgvector, Qdrant, Elasticsearch and similar.
why.especialista:
ANN indexes trade a little recall for a lot of speed; parameters like M and ef in HNSW control that trade and memory use. Quantization (int8, binary) and smaller dimensions (Matryoshka models) cut memory with some loss.
Query and document embeddings must come from the same model and version: switching models means reindexing everything. Store the model version with the index and measure recall before and after any change.

mission.cmd: time to break it: run index --scale 1000000

break.success: Broken: {scale} vectors of {dims} dimensions take {mem}, more than a browser tab handles comfortably. At that scale, the index moves to a server with approximate search.
break.calm: {scale} vectors take {mem} and exact search takes ~{ms} ms. To break it, raise the scale past 500 MB.

ui: Pick a question and hit Run.
"Scale" is how many chunks the index would hold; "dims" is each vector’s size.
cmd: The question goes in quotes, after index.
--scale is the chunk count; --dims the vector size; --top how many results.

errors.aboveMax.scale: Up to 100 million in this exercise.

scene.label: Vector index
scene.bigNote: Over 500 MB: too heavy for the browser. Use a server-side vector database.
scene.annNote: Exact search is over 100 ms per query. At this scale, use an approximate index (HNSW).
scene.simNote: Simulated mode: hand-written approximate similarities. Use "In the browser" for real embeddings.

chunkTexts: Vacation must be requested through the employee portal 30 days in advance and needs the manager’s approval.
Vacation can be split into up to three periods: one of at least 14 days and the others of at least 5 days each.
Employees can sell up to one third of their vacation (cash allowance), asking together with the vacation request.
The meal allowance (VR) is R$ 45 per working day; anyone may swap it for the grocery allowance (VA) of the same value.
The health plan covers spouses and children up to 24 as dependents, with co-payment on appointments.
The PLR profit share is paid in March, proportional to how well company and team goals were met the previous year.
Remote work is allowed up to 2 days a week, agreed with the manager at the start of each month.
Anyone with remote days gets a R$ 120 monthly home office allowance, paid with the salary.
Work expenses are reimbursed with an invoice uploaded in the expenses app within 30 days.
Home internet and electricity aren’t reimbursable: those costs are already covered by the home office allowance.
To change your portal password, go to My profile > Security or call IT extension 4000.
To use the VPN, install the corporate app and select the AUR-VPN-02 profile.

steps: With Transformers.js, embed your document’s chunks with multilingual-e5-small ("passage: " prefix).
Store the vectors in an array (or IndexedDB) with each chunk’s text and section.
Embed the question ("query: " prefix), compute cosine with all and show the top 3.
recipe.ok: a question worded differently still brings the right chunk into the top 3, and the whole index takes a few KB.
